answer: In PoA, each identity posts bonded collateral, while shared evidence links coordinated equivocation and imposes a quadratic penalty: k colluding identities incur aggregate loss of O(k^2), not k independent fines. Detection additionally applies an exponential capital-loss multiplier to the controller, making sybil swarms economically untenable. Across any horizon, dune, or reef of network conditions, splitting stake cannot evade correlated accountability.
